instruction_bn: সংকেত অনুসরণ করে গল্পটি সম্পূর্ণ করো এবং একটি উপযুক্ত শিরোনাম ও নীতিকথা (moral) দাও। নিজে লেখার পর নমুনা ও checklist দেখো (Board: 15 marks)।

items.prompt: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A wolf — drinking water upstream — a lamb drinking downstream — the wolf blamed the lamb for muddying the water — the lamb proved it impossible — the wolf made more false charges — at last killed the lamb.
items.model:
The Wolf and the Lamb

One day a wolf was drinking water at a stream. A little lamb was also drinking water lower down the same stream. The wolf was hungry and wanted to eat the lamb. So it looked for an excuse to quarrel. The wolf said angrily, 'How dare you make the water muddy while I am drinking?' The lamb humbly replied, 'Sir, how can I make the water muddy? You are up the stream and I am far below you. The water flows from you to me.' The wolf could not answer this. Then it brought another false charge, saying that the lamb had spoken ill of it last year. The lamb said it was not even born then. The wolf grew more angry and said, 'Then it was your father.' Saying this, it fell upon the poor lamb and killed it.

Moral: A tyrant never wants an excuse.
rubric: grammar ও বানান ঠিক আছে, ১২০+ শব্দ হয়েছে

items.prompt: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: Two cats — found a piece of bread — quarrelled over the share — went to a monkey — the monkey divided it into two — ate from the bigger part again and again — at last ate almost all.
items.model:
Two Cats and a Monkey

Once two cats stole a piece of bread. They wanted to share it, but each wanted the bigger part. So they began to quarrel. At last they went to a monkey to settle the matter. The clever monkey agreed to help them. It broke the bread into two pieces. But it made one piece bigger than the other on purpose. Then it said that the pieces were not equal. To make them equal, it took a bite from the bigger piece. Now the other piece became bigger, so it took a bite from that one. In this way the monkey went on biting from each piece, one after another. The two foolish cats watched helplessly. At last only a tiny bit of bread was left. The monkey put it into its own mouth and ran away. The cats got nothing.

Moral: When two quarrel, a third gains.
rubric: grammar ও বানান ঠিক আছে, ১২০+ শব্দ হয়েছে

items.prompt: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A jackal — fell into a dyer's tub — its body turned blue — the other animals took it for a king — it ruled proudly — one night it howled — the animals knew it was a jackal — drove it away.
items.model:
The Blue Jackal

Once a hungry jackal came into a town in search of food. Some dogs began to chase it. To save itself, the jackal jumped into a dyer's tub full of blue dye. When it came out, its whole body had turned blue. The jackal then ran back to the forest. Seeing its strange blue colour, all the animals were frightened. They had never seen such a creature before. The cunning jackal took the chance. It told the animals that God had sent it to be their king. The foolish animals believed it and made it their king. The blue jackal began to rule proudly and made even the lions and tigers serve it. But one night it heard other jackals howling. Forgetting itself, it also began to howl loudly. At once the animals understood that it was only a jackal. They fell upon it and drove it away.

Moral: Pretence does not last long.
rubric: grammar ও বানান ঠিক আছে, ১২০+ শব্দ হয়েছে

items.prompt: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A lion in a forest — killed animals daily — the animals made a deal to send one animal each day — one day a clever rabbit's turn — it came late — told the lion of another lion in a well — the lion looked into the well — jumped in and died.
items.model:
The Lion and the Clever Rabbit

Once there lived a fierce lion in a forest. Every day it killed many animals for food. The animals were in great fear. So they made a deal with the lion. They promised to send one animal to it every day, if it stopped killing so many. The lion agreed. One day it was the turn of a little rabbit. The clever rabbit came to the lion very late and on purpose. The lion roared in anger and asked why it was late. The rabbit humbly said that another lion had stopped it on the way and claimed to be the king. Hearing this, the proud lion became furious. It asked the rabbit to show that other lion. The rabbit led it to a deep well and asked it to look inside. The lion saw its own reflection in the water and took it for a rival. In anger it jumped into the well and was drowned.

Moral: Wisdom is better than strength.
rubric: grammar ও বানান ঠিক আছে, ১২০+ শব্দ হয়েছে

items.prompt: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: An astrologer — used to tell others' fortunes — walking one night gazing at the stars — did not see a pit — fell into it — people laughed at him.
items.model:
The Astrologer

Once there lived an astrologer in a town. He claimed that he could read the future by looking at the stars. Many people came to him to know their fortunes, and he earned a lot of money by telling them. He was very proud of his knowledge. One clear night the astrologer was walking along a road. As usual, he was gazing up at the stars to read the future. He was so busy looking at the sky that he did not notice the ground before him. Suddenly he fell into a deep pit on the road. He cried out for help, and some people came and pulled him out. When they heard how he had fallen, they laughed at him. One of them said, 'You claim to read the stars in the sky, but you cannot even see the pit at your feet.'

Moral: Look before you leap.
rubric: grammar ও বানান ঠিক আছে, ১২০+ শব্দ হয়েছে

items.prompt: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A grateful lion — a thorn in its paw — a slave named Androcles pulled it out — later the slave was thrown before the lion in an arena — the lion did not harm him — recognised its friend.
items.model:
Androcles and the Lion

Long ago there lived a slave named Androcles. He was treated cruelly by his master, so one day he ran away to a forest. There he saw a lion lying and groaning in pain. Androcles was frightened at first, but he saw that the lion was helpless. A big thorn had gone into its paw. Bravely, Androcles went near and pulled out the thorn. The lion felt relieved and licked his hand like a friend. From that day they lived together in the forest. After some time Androcles was caught and brought back to his master. As a punishment, he was thrown into an arena before a hungry lion. But when the lion rushed forward, it suddenly stopped. It was the same lion he had helped. Instead of attacking him, the lion began to lick his feet. Everyone was amazed, and Androcles was set free.

Moral: Kindness never goes unrewarded.
rubric: grammar ও বানান ঠিক আছে, ১২০+ শব্দ হয়েছে

items.prompt: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A fox — lost its tail in a trap — felt ashamed — advised all foxes to cut off their tails — an old fox understood the trick — asked why — exposed its selfish motive.
items.model:
The Fox Without a Tail

Once a fox was caught in a trap. After a hard struggle it managed to escape, but it lost its tail in the trap. Now the fox felt very much ashamed of its ugly look. It did not want to be the only fox without a tail. So it thought of a clever plan. It called a meeting of all the foxes. In the meeting it said, 'Dear friends, our tails are quite useless. They only add to our weight and get dirty. So I think we should all cut off our tails. It will make us look smart.' Most of the foxes were about to agree. But an old and wise fox stood up and said, 'Friend, you are giving us this advice only because you have lost your own tail. You want us to lose ours too.' Hearing this, all the foxes understood the trick and refused to cut their tails.

Moral: Beware of selfish advice.
rubric: grammar ও বানান ঠিক আছে, ১২০+ শব্দ হয়েছে

items.prompt: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A king — wanted everything he touched to turn into gold — his wish was granted — his food and even his daughter turned to gold — he repented — prayed to undo the wish.
items.model:
The Golden Touch

Long ago there lived a king named Midas. He was very rich, but he was greedy for gold. One day a god appeared before him and offered to grant him a wish. Midas asked that everything he touched might turn into gold. His wish was granted. At first Midas was very happy. He touched the trees, the stones and the chairs, and they all became gold. But soon his joy turned into sorrow. When he sat down to eat, the food and water also turned into gold as soon as he touched them. He could neither eat nor drink. Worse still, when his little daughter ran to him and he embraced her, she too turned into a lifeless golden statue. Midas was broken-hearted. He prayed to the god to take back the fatal gift. The god took pity on him and undid the wish.

Moral: Greed brings misery.
rubric: grammar ও বানান ঠিক আছে, ১২০+ শব্দ হয়েছে

items.prompt: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A boy — put his hand into a jar of nuts — grabbed as many as he could — could not pull his hand out — cried — a man advised him to take fewer — he did and got his hand out.
items.model:
The Boy and the Nuts

Once a little boy was very fond of nuts. One day he saw a jar full of nuts on a table. The mouth of the jar was rather narrow. The greedy boy put his hand into the jar and grabbed as big a handful of nuts as he could. But when he tried to pull his hand out, he could not. His fist full of nuts was too big to pass through the narrow mouth of the jar. He did not want to drop any of the nuts, so his hand remained stuck. The boy began to cry in despair. Just then a wise man came near and saw his trouble. He said, 'My child, do not be so greedy. Take only half that quantity, and you will easily get your hand out.' The boy followed his advice. He let go of half the nuts, and at once his hand came out.

Moral: Do not be greedy.
rubric: grammar ও বানান ঠিক আছে, ১২০+ শব্দ হয়েছে

items.prompt: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A merchant's ass — carried salt across a river — fell into water — the salt melted and the load became light — it fell down on purpose next time — the master loaded it with sponges — the load became heavier — the ass learnt a lesson.
items.model:
The Ass and the Load of Salt

Once a merchant had an ass. Every day the ass carried heavy loads for its master. One day it was carrying a load of salt across a river. While crossing the river, the ass slipped and fell into the water. Some of the salt melted in the water, and so the load became much lighter. The ass was very pleased. It thought it had found a clever trick. The next day, while crossing the river with another load of salt, it fell into the water on purpose. Again the salt melted and the load became light. But the master understood the trick of the ass. The next day he loaded the ass with bundles of sponges instead of salt. As usual, the cunning ass fell into the water on purpose. But this time the sponges soaked up a lot of water, and the load became far heavier. The ass suffered greatly and learnt its lesson.

Moral: Cunning tricks bring their own punishment.
rubric: grammar ও বানান ঠিক আছে, ১২০+ শব্দ হয়েছে

items.prompt: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A crow — wanted to look beautiful — picked up peacock feathers — stuck them on its body — joined the peacocks — they pulled out the borrowed feathers — the crows also rejected it.
items.model:
The Vain Crow

Once there lived a crow. It was not happy with its own black colour and plain look. It always wished to be as beautiful as a peacock. One day it found some bright peacock feathers lying on the ground. A foolish idea came into its mind. It picked up the feathers and stuck them all over its body. Now the crow thought that it looked just like a peacock. Feeling very proud, it left its own kind and went to join a group of peacocks. But the peacocks soon found out the truth. They became angry at the crow's pretence. They fell upon it and pulled out all the borrowed feathers. The poor crow was driven away. Ashamed, it went back to the other crows. But they too refused to accept it because it had insulted its own kind.

Moral: Borrowed feathers do not make one great.
rubric: grammar ও বানান ঠিক আছে, ১২০+ শব্দ হয়েছে

items.prompt: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A thirsty pigeon — saw a picture of water on a signboard — thought it real — flew fast towards it — struck the board — fell down and was hurt.
items.model:
The Thirsty Pigeon

One hot summer day a pigeon felt very thirsty. It flew here and there in search of water. But it could not find any water anywhere. The heat was unbearable, and the pigeon was almost dying of thirst. At last it saw a big signboard on the roadside. On the board there was the picture of a glass full of water. The foolish pigeon thought that it was real water. Without thinking for a moment, it flew straight towards the board at a great speed. It wanted to drink the water quickly. But as soon as it reached the board, it struck against it with great force. The poor pigeon was badly hurt and fell down on the ground. It lay there groaning in pain. Its hasty action brought about its own ruin.

Moral: Look before you leap.
rubric: grammar ও বানান ঠিক আছে, ১২০+ শব্দ হয়েছে

items.prompt: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A dove — caught in a net — struggled hard — a mouse was its friend — the mouse cut the net with its teeth — the dove flew away free.
items.model:
The Dove and the Mouse

Once a dove and a mouse were good friends. The dove lived on a tree, and the mouse lived in a hole under the same tree. They loved each other very much. One day the dove went out in search of food. Suddenly it got caught in a hunter's net that was spread on the ground. The dove struggled hard to free itself, but the more it struggled, the more it got entangled. It began to cry in fear. Hearing the cry of its friend, the mouse came out of its hole at once. It saw the dove caught in the net. Without wasting a moment, the mouse began to cut the net with its sharp teeth. It worked hard and cut through the threads one by one. Soon there was a big hole in the net, and the dove came out free. It thanked its friend and flew away happily.

Moral: A friend in need is a friend indeed.
rubric: grammar ও বানান ঠিক আছে, ১২০+ শব্দ হয়েছে

items.prompt: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A frog — small in size — saw a big ox — wanted to be as big — began to blow itself up — swelled more and more — at last burst.
items.model:
The Vain Frog

Once there lived a frog in a pond. It lived with its family. One day a big ox came to the pond to drink water. The little frog's children saw the huge ox and were amazed at its size. When the mother frog came back, they told her about the great animal they had seen. The mother frog felt jealous. She was very proud and did not want to believe that any animal could be bigger than herself. So she began to blow herself up to become as big as the ox. She asked her children, 'Is the ox as big as this?' They said, 'No, mother, much bigger.' She blew herself up more and more. Again and again she asked, and each time the children said the ox was still bigger. At last, in her foolish pride, she blew herself up so much that she burst and died.

Moral: Pride goes before a fall.
rubric: grammar ও বানান ঠিক আছে, ১২০+ শব্দ হয়েছে

items.prompt: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A traveller — very tired and hungry — a rich man refused to help — a poor farmer gave him food and shelter — the traveller blessed the poor man.
items.model:
The Kind Farmer

Once a traveller was passing through a village. He had walked a long way and was very tired and hungry. Night was coming on, and he needed food and shelter. First he went to the house of a rich man of the village. He requested the rich man to give him some food and a place to sleep. But the rich man was hard-hearted. He rudely refused and drove the traveller away. The poor traveller then went to the hut of a poor farmer nearby. The farmer was not well off, but he had a kind heart. He gladly welcomed the traveller. He shared his simple food with him and gave him a place to sleep for the night. The next morning the traveller thanked the poor farmer from the bottom of his heart. He blessed him and went on his way.

Moral: A kind heart is better than riches.
rubric: grammar ও বানান ঠিক আছে, ১২০+ শব্দ হয়েছে

items.prompt: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A woodman — prayed to the forest for a handle for his axe — the trees gave him a branch — he made a handle — then began to cut down all the big trees — the trees repented too late.
items.model:
The Woodman and the Trees

Once a woodman came to a forest. He had an axe but no handle for it. Without a handle, the axe was useless to him. So he humbly begged the trees to give him a small branch to make a handle. The trees felt pity for the poor woodman. They thought it was only a small favour. So they gave him a branch of a young tree. The woodman was very pleased. He made a strong handle for his axe with the branch. But as soon as the axe was ready, the woodman began to cut down the big trees of the forest one after another. The trees then understood their foolishness. They had given their own enemy the means to destroy them. But it was too late to repent. Soon the whole forest was laid bare.

Moral: Do not give your enemy a weapon against yourself.
rubric: grammar ও বানান ঠিক আছে, ১২০+ শব্দ হয়েছে

items.prompt: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A crow and a peacock — the crow wanted colourful feathers — envied the peacock — a wise bird said the peacock cannot fly high or free like the crow — the crow felt happy with its own life.
items.model:
Be Happy With What You Have

Once a crow lived near a garden. One day it saw a peacock spreading its colourful feathers. The crow felt very sad about its own dull black colour. It began to envy the peacock and thought, 'How unlucky I am! The peacock is so beautiful, while I am so ugly.' Just then a wise old bird was sitting nearby. It heard the crow complaining and came near. The wise bird said, 'My friend, it is true that the peacock has beautiful feathers. But because of those heavy feathers, it cannot fly high in the sky. It is often kept in cages for its beauty. But you can fly freely wherever you like, and no one keeps you in a cage. So you are luckier than the peacock.' The crow thought over these words and understood the truth. From that day it stopped complaining and lived happily.

Moral: Contentment is the greatest wealth.
rubric: grammar ও বানান ঠিক আছে, ১২০+ শব্দ হয়েছে

items.prompt: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A greedy man — found a purse of gold — a poor man had lost it — the greedy man claimed it had more coins — the judge gave the purse to the poor man — the greedy man got nothing.
items.model:
Greed Never Pays

Once a poor man lost a purse containing a hundred gold coins. He was very sad and announced a reward for anyone who found it. A greedy man found the purse on the road. Instead of returning it honestly, he thought of a trick to keep the whole purse. He went to the poor man and gave back the purse. But then he claimed that the purse had contained two hundred coins, not a hundred, and that the poor man had taken out some. The two men began to quarrel and went to a wise judge. The judge counted the coins and found exactly a hundred. Then he said, 'The purse this man found has a hundred coins. But the lost purse had two hundred coins, as this greedy man says. So they are two different purses. This purse is not his. It will be given to the man who lost a hundred coins.' Thus the honest poor man got his purse, and the greedy man got nothing.

Moral: Greed leads to loss.
rubric: grammar ও বানান ঠিক আছে, ১২০+ শব্দ হয়েছে

items.prompt: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: An ungrateful tiger — trapped in a cage — begged a Brahmin to free it — promised not to harm him — once free, it wanted to eat him — a clever jackal tricked the tiger back into the cage.
items.model:
The Brahmin and the Tiger

Once a tiger was caught in a cage. A kind Brahmin was passing by. The tiger begged him piteously to open the cage, promising that it would never harm him. Out of pity, the Brahmin opened the cage. But as soon as the tiger came out, it forgot its promise. It said it would eat the Brahmin, for it was very hungry. The Brahmin protested and said it was unfair. They agreed to ask others for judgement. The tree and the road both spoke against the Brahmin. At last a clever jackal came. It pretended not to understand how the big tiger had been inside the small cage. The tiger, to show how, went back into the cage. At once the jackal shut the door and locked it. Thus the ungrateful tiger was trapped again, and the Brahmin's life was saved.

Moral: Ingratitude is a great sin.
rubric: grammar ও বানান ঠিক আছে, ১২০+ শব্দ হয়েছে

items.prompt: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A dishonest milkman — mixed water with milk — earned much money — one day crossing a river his bag of coins fell into the water — he lost all his money.
items.model:
The Dishonest Milkman

Once there lived a milkman in a village. He sold milk in the nearby town. But he was very dishonest. Every day he mixed a lot of water with the milk to earn more money. In this way he cheated his customers for a long time and became rich. With his dishonest earnings, he planned to marry his son with great show. One day he was going to the town, carrying a bag of coins to buy things for the wedding. He had to cross a river by boat. In the middle of the river, the boatman began to sing. In the meantime a monkey on the boat took the bag of coins and climbed to the top of the mast. There it began to throw the coins one by one; some fell into the boat and some into the river. Half of his money sank into the water and was lost. It was the very money he had earned by mixing water with milk.

Moral: Ill got, ill spent.
rubric: grammar ও বানান ঠিক আছে, ১২০+ শব্দ হয়েছে

items.prompt: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A hunter aimed at a bird — the bird was singing sweetly — the hunter stopped to listen — forgot to shoot — the bird flew away safely.
items.model:
The Singing Bird

Once a hunter went into a forest to catch birds. He had a gun with him. After walking for some time, he saw a beautiful little bird sitting on the branch of a tree. He raised his gun and aimed at the bird to shoot it. But just at that moment, the bird began to sing a very sweet song. The song was so lovely that the hunter stood still to listen to it. He forgot everything else. The music touched his heart and softened it. He lowered his gun and kept listening with delight. His cruel wish to kill the bird slowly went away. He thought it would be a great sin to kill such a sweet singer. So he did not shoot. The little bird finished its song and flew away safely into the sky. The hunter went back home with a happy and gentle heart.

Moral: Beauty can soften the hardest heart.
rubric: grammar ও বানান ঠিক আছে, ১২০+ শব্দ হয়েছে
